cases.title: Matrix transformations: an eigenvector lesson
cases.description: An explanation and worked example of matrix eigenvectors.
cases.text: An eigenvector of a matrix A is a nonzero vector v for which Av equals lambda times v. The transformation may stretch or reverse the vector, but its direction lies on the same line. Lambda is the eigenvalue. For example, let A be the diagonal matrix with entries 2 and 3. Multiplying the vector (1, 0) by A gives (2, 0), so (1, 0) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 2. Multiplying (0, 1) gives (0, 3), so (0, 1) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 3. A vector that changes direction under A is not an eigenvector of A.
